subject: Re: Proof-of-Fit: Trial success criteria, remediation plan, and owners
thread_summary: Post-discovery recap capturing trial success criteria, immediate blockers (S3 access + schema mismatch), assigned owners, mitigation steps and an agreed 2-week timeline for unblock and trial kickoff. Next: technical deep-dive Wednesday and updated trial plan by Friday.
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@novus-retail.com>, Oscar Ruiz <oscar.ruiz@novus-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proof-of-Fit recap + proposed success criteria and next steps

Thanks for the call this morning — great conversation and clear alignment on business goals. Per our discussion, I’m sending a concise recap and the proposed trial success criteria so we can de-risk the pilot before we spin up dedicated nodes. Please review and confirm owners for the items below.

High-level objective:
- Validate that Redwood can deliver 95th percentile generation latency < 350ms for 512-token inference on your peak query slice, and that accuracy (top-1 match to in-house label set) meets your internal threshold for product catalog extraction.

Proposed trial success criteria (actionable, measurable):
1) Latency: 95th percentile <= 350ms for the 512-token baseline pattern (sample set we discussed). Measurement window: 72h synthetic + 24h organic.
2) Quality: F1 >= 0.82 on our shared 2k prompt-label set for product title normalization.
3) Reliability: <= 2% error rate (timeouts/alerts) across the week-long run.
4) Integration: automated S3 ingest & schema mapping with <2 schema exceptions after remediation.

Immediate blockers we flagged:
- Novus S3 read access is not yet configured for redwood-trials@redwood.ai (Oscar to confirm IAM policy).
- Sample schema has nested category arrays; our onboarding connector expects a flat category field (dev mapping needed).

Proposed owners & timeline (suggested):
- Oscar Ruiz (Novus) — provision S3 read role for redwood-trials@redwood.ai by Fri 6/18 EOD.
- Dev Patel (Redwood) — prepare a lightweight ingest adapter to flatten category arrays; target PR and deployment to staging by Tue 6/22.
- Marissa Cole (Redwood CS) — coordinate daily check-ins during the first test window and maintain the issue tracker.
- Ben Carter (Redwood AE) — commercial point for any scope/term changes.

Attachments: trial-success-metrics-v1.xlsx (metrics and measurement plan), novus-data-ingest-checklist.pdf (what we need from the S3 bucket).

Next steps (please reply with confirmations/changes):
1) Oscar: confirm S3 role and any org security constraints by Thu 6/17.
2) Dev: confirm dev timeline and whether we need a sample dataset back-and-forth.
3) All: schedule the technical deep-dive (60m) — we proposed Wed 6/16 10:00am PT.

Thanks — I’ll update the shared doc with any edits.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

---

From: Lara Chen <lara.chen@novus-retail.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oscar Ruiz <oscar.ruiz@novus-retail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proof-of-Fit recap + proposed success criteria and next steps

Thanks Naomi — solid write-up. A few clarifications from our side:

1) S3 access: I can provision the role but will need a short justification string for our security team. Oscar and I will confirm the exact IAM policy by end of day Thursday. We cannot expose full read across prod buckets; we’ll provision a scoped staging bucket.

2) Schema: The category nesting is present only in the new catalog export (staging). We can provide a flattened sample CSV for the first two days to unblock ingestion while we work on the adapter.

3) Latency expectations: 350ms 95th is aggressive for our heavier catalog items. Can the trial include a small long-tail carve-out (e.g., items > 1k tokens) excluded from the SLA so we can focus on the core 80% traffic?

4) Compliance: we will need confirmation that Redwood will not cache PII fields and that audit logs will be available for the trial.

We’ll join Wed 6/16 10am PT for the deep-dive.

Best,
Lara Chen
Head of Data Platforms | Novus Retail
lara.chen@novus-retail.com

On Tue, Jun 15, 2027 at 09:12 Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (original message above)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@novus-retail.com>, Oscar Ruiz <oscar.ruiz@novus-retail.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proof-of-Fit recap + proposed success criteria and next steps

Appreciate the rapid replies — quick responses inline and commitments so we have a clear remediation path.

Lara / Oscar: thanks for the constraints on S3. Naomi — can you prepare a one-paragraph justification for the security team that Oscar can paste in the ticket? We’ll accept scope-limited staged bucket access.

On the SLA carve-out for long-tail items: absolutely reasonable. Proposal: we run two slices in parallel during the week-long run — core 80% (SLA targets apply) and long-tail 20% (no SLA, data used for quality analysis only). Naomi / Dev, please reflect that in the measurement sheet.

Compliance / caching: Naomi, can you confirm Redwood’s default behavior for PII during trials? We should surface the audit log retention settings and whether we can turn off any persistence for trial-only buckets. Marissa — can you prepare a short compliance note and link to SOC2 docs ahead of Wed?

Owners & updated timeline: 
- Oscar Ruiz (Novus) — scoped staging bucket role to redwood-trials@redwood.ai by Thu 6/17 EOD (confirm ticket ID in reply).
- Dev Patel (Redwood) — adapt ingest adapter and ship a staging PR by Tue 6/22; will also provide a short script to flatten the sample CSV if needed earlier.
- Naomi Feldman (Redwood) — update the trial measurement sheet with core/long-tail slices and provide the security justification paragraph by Wed 6/16 AM.
- Marissa Cole (Redwood) — compliance note and SOC2 evidence link by Wed 6/16 AM.

I’ve attached a short commercial note with trial credits and a conservative estimate for Dedicated throughput if you want to see numbers post-trial (attachment: trial-success-metrics-v1.xlsx).

Next sync: Wed 6/16 10:00am PT — technical deep-dive (60m). Agenda to include: S3 mapping, ingest adapter design, measurement plan, and minimal acceptance gates for go/no-go.

If any of the owners cannot meet these dates, flag now so we can re-sequence.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0178

From: Oscar Ruiz <oscar.ruiz@novus-retail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lara Chen <lara.chen@novus-retail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 13:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proof-of-Fit recap + proposed success criteria and next steps

Thanks — confirming next steps from my side:
- I will create a scoped staging bucket and open a ticket with our security team by EOD Thu 6/17. Ticket will include the justification paragraph once Naomi sends it.
- We will export a flattened sample CSV for the first 48h of trial data to speed onboarding; will upload to the staging bucket by Mon 6/21.
- Regarding audit logs/PII: our security team will expect a written compliance note from Redwood — Naomi/Marissa please include the SOC2 link and whether logs are delivered as part of the trial.

We’re fine with the core/long-tail split for SLA. Wed 10am PT works for our engineers.

Oscar Ruiz
Director, Data Engineering | Novus Retail
oscar.ruiz@novus-retail.com
